# Phase 5 manager acceptance

Accepted exact candidate `8c328b900f9e9733d6153e2efdc6a0b35cc6673b` and integrated locally by fast-forward. The worktree was clean; the only change after the verified implementation revision `ab67dc2` was the inspected phase report. No remote publication occurred.

Manager independently observed the pinned full gate: typecheck, 35 test files / 289 tests, Console and TypeScript builds, and clean temporary packed-CLI installation, session32717 exit0. Earlier focused assembled runtime verification passed 32 tests in six files, session24076. Localhost-dependent tests used the normal approved execution gate; sandbox listen denial was not treated as a product failure.

The implementer supplied observed browser evidence for the four Console views, shared filters, hierarchy and dependencies, supported permission responses, resource separation, live state updates and admission pause/resume, with empty browser diagnostics. Manager inspected the actual service/startup/UI composition and returned concrete gaps before acceptance: production fixtures, blocking command serialization, stale replay receipts, missing live updates, missing hierarchy/filter/request controls, and a GM configuration that could not diagnose new events. The final runtime uses the shipped provider routes and bounded dynamic diagnosis template; fixtures remain test seams.

This acceptance covers Phase5, not whole-system release. Live provider authentication evidence remains from earlier phases; these new integration checks used deterministic transports. Recovery, backup/updates, cold-start installation and final comparative/Twinzy proof remain Phase6/7 work.

Efficiency lesson: assess the cost of accepted work, not initial model price. Terra's incomplete composition required Sol-high remediation. Begin consequential cross-module integration with a sufficiently capable orchestrator; use cheaper specialists for bounded ownership. Verify installed paths and substantive acceptance before broad repeated gates. Phase estimates remain advisory and must never become native goal caps; the owner's remaining account allowance is binding.
